soil-class-157.q: Why are constructed soils preferred to imported topsoil?
soil-class-157.a: Harvesting topsoil degrades a second site and usually costs more.

soil-class-167.q: When was this quicksand without water first created in the laboratory?
soil-class-167.a: In 2004, after long being doubted as folklore.

soil-fert-190.q: Who should avoid soil with estimated total lead above 300 ppm?

soil-fert-164.q: At what concentration in soil water is boron toxic to most plants?

soil-fert-186.q: What carbon-to-nitrogen ratios point to marine sources, and what to land plants?
soil-fert-186.a: Ratios of 4-10:1 usually mean marine sources, while land vascular plants tend to exceed 20.

soil-fert-195.q: What do preplant and late-spring soil nitrogen tests show?
soil-fert-195.a: Preplant tests show the soil's nitrogen-supplying power, and late-spring or pre-side-dress tests decide whether more is needed.

soil-fert-229.q: How does manganese deficiency show on leaves, and which leaves first?
soil-fert-229.a: Leaves yellow between the veins in a chequered pattern; young leaves show it first because manganese is immobile.

soil-fert-291.q: Which rotations leach less nitrogen than annual row crops?
soil-fert-291.a: Rotations with cover crops, perennial grasses and legumes.

soil-fert-284.q: How does copper deficiency show in plants?
soil-fert-284.a: As browning of leaf tips and chlorosis.

soil-fert-292.q: What do slow-release nitrogen forms and inhibitors do?
soil-fert-292.a: They better match nitrogen supply to crop needs.

soil-found-066.q: In which three oxidation states does mercury occur?

soil-fert-128.q: What limits how much phosphorus an ecosystem has?
soil-fert-128.a: The rate at which weathering releases phosphorus; apatite dissolution is a key control on productivity.

soil-fert-117.q: Who first suggested, and when, that oxidizing ammonia to nitrate is biological?

soil-fert-224.q: How does urea hydrolysis change the pH around it?
soil-fert-224.a: It raises it, because the basic ammonia released is produced in two stages through carbamic acid.

soil-fert-221.q: What view did Nitrospira inopinata overturn?
soil-fert-221.a: That the two steps of nitrification need two organisms; it carries out complete nitrification (comammox).

soil-fert-279.q: What is a farm with a negative nutrient balance doing?
soil-fert-279.a: Living off capital, drawing down mineral and organic-matter nutrients until yields fall.

soil-fert-225.q: Which organisms can turn N2O into N2?
soil-fert-225.a: Only denitrifying prokaryotes, though some denitrifiers lack the step and stop at N2O.

soil-fert-277.q: What is the optimum nitrogen balance, and what do values below 0 and above 50 mean?
soil-fert-277.a: Generally between 0 and +50 pounds per acre; below 0 the soil is being mined of nitrogen, and above 50 the excess causes environmental damage.

soil-fert-035.q: How is compost tea usually made?
soil-fert-035.a: By adding compost to water at 1:4-1:10 and stirring occasionally to release microbes, with or without aeration.

soil-fert-033.q: Why does stabilized compost pose very little risk?
soil-fert-033.a: It has reached 50-70 °C, which kills pathogens and makes even oocysts unviable.

soil-fert-081.q: Which seaweeds are used most, and in what forms?
soil-fert-081.a: Brown seaweeds; laid as mulch, composted, dried and powdered, or made into liquid extracts.

soil-fert-077.q: What did a 2013 study find about a single compost application on grassland?
soil-fert-077.a: It significantly and durably raised carbon storage by 25-70%.

soil-fert-083.q: Which has the highest salt index: potassium chloride, urea or diammonium phosphate?
soil-fert-083.a: Potassium chloride, at 116.2, against 74.4 for urea and 29.2 for diammonium phosphate.

soil-fert-262.q: By how much does a compost pile shrink?
soil-fert-262.a: By 30-60 percent as carbon dioxide and water escape.

soil-fert-205.q: As of 2016, did any country have a specific regulatory framework for biostimulants?
soil-fert-205.a: No; with no agreed definition, some treat them under fertilizer law.

soil-fert-274.q: What should be cut first when phosphorus surpluses build up on livestock farms?
soil-fert-274.a: P in animal diets; a survey found US dairy herds fed about 25% more P than NRC advice.

soil-fert-216.q: What factor converts P2O5 to elemental phosphorus, and K2O to potassium?
soil-fert-216.a: P2O5 is 43.6% phosphorus, so multiply by 0.436; K2O is 83% potassium, so multiply by 0.83.

soil-fert-240.q: What are the two types of integrated crop-livestock farm?
soil-fert-240.a: One mainly sells animal products and matches animal numbers to carrying capacity; the other is a diversified farm that raises all its feed but sells a range of crops and animal products.

soil-fert-268.q: What is the late-spring nitrate test especially good at identifying?
soil-fert-268.a: Sites that need no more N fertilizer, since it implicitly captures early-season weather.

soil-fert-249.q: What should be done where soil P is far above optimum?
soil-fert-249.a: Apply manure by crop P need and export part of it.
